Hi,
I am new one in this group and also new user of lavaan package. When I done this 'fit <- cfa(psqi.model, data=psqui_fa)' on my data R reply this warnings 'Warning message:
In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative'
Is that some strange in data? What happens?
Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lav_object_post_check(lavobject)
parts: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative'

That is called a Heywood case, and you can find some reading about it on Google, SEMNET, or any introductory SEM textbook.  Here is an article about testing whether it is cause for alarm:

http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0049124112442138

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lav_object_post_check(lavobject)
parts: is it possible to do that with polycoric correlation in lavaan packaga and draw the diagram?

You can ask general SEM questions on the SEMNET forum

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

but yes, if your indicators are only 4 categories (0, 1, 2, 3), then you can treat them appropriately as ordinal data using DWLS estimation in lavaan:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
